user.title: Set up B-Hyve
user.description: Sign in to the Orbit cloud to find your timers, or set up without it. Either way the timers are controlled locally over Bluetooth; the cloud is only used to fetch device IDs and network keys.

menu_options.local_manual: Enter a timer by hand (no cloud)

cloud.title: B-Hyve account
cloud.description: Sign in with your Orbit B-Hyve cloud account. The integration uses cloud only at setup time to fetch device IDs and network keys, then talks to each timer over BLE — no cloud round trip after setup.

local_import.title: Import devices (no cloud)
local_import.description: Paste the response of the orbit_bhyve.export_devices action (YAML or JSON), or a list of device records. Every timer in it is added. {detail}

local_manual.title: Add a timer (no cloud)
local_manual.description: Enter one timer; add more later with Reconfigure. The network key is the 16-byte Orbit mesh key (32 hex characters or base64). HT25-0000 mesh timers also need their mesh device ID, and should get their hub's mesh ID: if it's blank, every connect writes 0x0000 as the timer's hub ID, which can cut it off from the B-Hyve hub and app. IDs are decimal or 0x hex. {detail}

pick_devices.title: Discovered devices
pick_devices.description: Found {count} device(s). Uncheck any you don't want HA to manage.

reauth_confirm.title: B-Hyve — re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: Your saved Orbit credentials no longer authenticate. Enter the password again.

reconfigure_auth.title: B-Hyve — confirm password
reconfigure_auth.description: The saved password for {email} was rejected by the Orbit cloud. Enter it again to re-run device discovery.

reconfigure.title: Update B-Hyve devices (no cloud)
reconfigure.description: This entry was set up without an Orbit account.

menu_options.reconfigure_manual: Add or edit a timer by hand

reconfigure_manual.title: Add or edit a timer
reconfigure_manual.description: A MAC address that's already in this entry replaces that timer's settings. The network key is prefilled when the entry has only one. HT25-0000 mesh timers need their mesh device ID and should get their hub's mesh ID (blank writes 0x0000 as the hub ID on every connect). IDs are decimal or 0x hex. {detail}

reconfigure_import.title: Import more devices
reconfigure_import.description: Paste an export_devices response or a list of device records. Timers already in this entry are updated in place. {detail}

reconfigure_keep.title: Timers to keep
reconfigure_keep.description: Uncheck a timer to remove it and its entities.

reconfigure_devices.title: Update B-Hyve devices
reconfigure_devices.description: Re-queried the Orbit cloud: {count} device(s), {new} new, {missing} no longer on the account. New devices are pre-checked; devices you excluded before stay unchecked. Devices marked "no longer on the Orbit account" keep working over BLE while they stay checked — uncheck one to remove it and its entities. If this is the first time you have reconfigured this entry, devices you excluded during the original setup may reappear checked: the entry never recorded them. Uncheck them once and the choice sticks.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Orbit cloud API. Check your network connection.
error.no_devices: Login succeeded but no devices were found on this account.
error.no_devices_selected: Select at least one device — an empty selection would disable the integration.
error.invalid_import: Couldn't read the export: expected YAML or JSON holding device records. {detail}
error.invalid_key: Invalid network key ({detail}): expected 32 hex characters or base64 for 16 bytes.
error.invalid_mesh_id: Invalid mesh ID ({detail}): expected a number from 0 to 65535, decimal or 0x hex.
error.mesh_id_required: HT25-0000 mesh timers need a mesh device ID ({detail}).
error.duplicate_mac: The same MAC address appears twice ({detail}).
error.mac_already_configured: {detail} is already set up in another B-Hyve entry.

abort.already_configured: This Orbit account or network is already configured.
abort.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Orbit cloud API. Nothing was changed — try again later.
abort.no_devices: The Orbit cloud returned no devices for this account. Nothing was changed.
abort.unknown: Unexpected error re-querying the Orbit cloud. Nothing was changed.

data.mesh_status_poll: Mesh live status poll — HT25 connects over BLE on each idle poll to read watering state and battery (costs battery: ~96 connects/day at the default cadence)
data.hub_mesh_overrides: Hub mesh ID overrides — optional, only if the cloud doesn't report your hub's mesh ID. Comma-separated MAC=id pairs, decimal or 0x-hex (e.g. "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF=0xEB42"). Leave blank unless watering commands are being dropped.

start_watering.name: Start watering
start_watering.description: Start watering on a specific zone for a given duration.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long to water, in seconds.

stop_all.name: Stop all
stop_all.description: Stop all watering on the targeted device.

refresh_devices.name: Refresh devices from cloud
refresh_devices.description: Re-query the Orbit cloud and merge the result into the config entry: adds newly-discovered devices, keeps devices you excluded excluded, and never overwrites a working network key or mesh ID with a blank one.

config_entry_id.name: Account
config_entry_id.description: Which B-Hyve account to refresh. Omit to refresh every configured account.

export_devices.name: Export devices
export_devices.description: Return every configured timer's record, network key included, so the integration can be set up again without the Orbit cloud (Add integration → Import). The network key controls every timer on the account; keep the export somewhere safe. Admin only.

config_entry_id.name: Account
config_entry_id.description: Which entries to export. Omit to export all of them.

recover_firmware.name: Recover firmware (HT25-0000)
recover_firmware.description: Re-send the official firmware to an HT25-0000 hose timer stuck in its bootloader (blinking white) after a failed update. Works on a timer that is no longer on your account. Refuses any timer that is not in its bootloader, and only sends an image matching a known-good hash. Runs in the background; progress appears as a notification. Only verified on HT25-0000 with fw0085.

config_entry_id.name: Account
config_entry_id.description: Which saved B-Hyve login downloads the firmware. Omit to use the first one.

set_program.name: Set watering program
set_program.description: Create or replace a watering program (slots A–D) on a B-Hyve valve (HT34A / HT25G2).

day_mode.name: Day mode
day_mode.description: How often the program runs. Exactly one mode.

weekdays.name: Weekdays
weekdays.description: For day mode "weekdays" — which days to run.

interval_days.name: Interval (days)
interval_days.description: For day mode "interval" — run every N days.

interval_anchor.name: Interval anchor date
interval_anchor.description: For day mode "interval" — ISO date the interval counts from (default today).

start_times.name: Start times
start_times.description: One or more start times (HH:MM, device-local).

zones.name: Zones
zones.description: Per-zone run time — a list of zone/minutes pairs.

name.name: Program name
name.description: Optional label stored on the device (max 32 bytes; longer names are rejected by the device).

enabled.name: Enable
enabled.description: Enable and arm the program so it runs on schedule.

delete_program.name: Delete watering program
delete_program.description: Clear a watering program slot (A–D) on a B-Hyve valve (HT34A / HT25G2).

get_program.name: Get watering program(s)
get_program.description: Read back the stored watering programs (A–D) from a B-Hyve valve (HT34A / HT25G2).

slot.name: Program slot
slot.description: Optional — a single slot (A–D). Omit to return all slots.
